proof:
Source: step 4(a)-(b) of the parent proof ('measure on the graph' via (M.iv), (UD), (F2); 'tangent planes' via (F1) and (Area)), stated as a single comparison inequality; the tangent-plane identification along the Lipschitz graph is proved directly by blowing up through the area formula.

Notation. mu := V.weight = theta H^n restricted to M (M := V.carrier, theta := V.mult), spt V := V.support, p_w := V.tangentProj w, omega_n := unitBallVolume n. Given q, f, R as in the statement: F(x) := q(graphPoint x (f x)) for x in R^n; Gamma_R := q '' graphOver f (B^n_R(0)); for a linear map A : R^n -> R^l, Pi_q(A) := starProjection of (span{graphPoint v (A v)}).map q, the orthogonal projection onto the n-plane q(graph A). Then the left integrand of the statement is Phi(F(x), Pi_q(Df(x))) with Df(x) := fderiv f x.
Facts used. (P.ii) [sibling allard52_density_bounds] for the given n and p there are delta_P in (0, 1/8] and C_P > 0 with C_P delta_P <= 1/2, depending only on n and p (the same for every codimension l), such that under 2.3 with delta <= delta_P, if y in spt V, |y| <= 3 delta rho and 0 < s <= rho/2 then mu(B_s(y)) >= (1 - C_P delta) omega_n s^n >= omega_n s^n/2. (T) [sibling allard52_tangent_ae] p is mu-a.e. strongly measurable. (UD) [Simon Ch. 1, Thm 3.2(1); SimonGMT Chapter01.mul_simonHausdorff_le_of_le_dimensionalUpperDensity] if nu is a Borel regular measure and Theta^{*n}(nu, x) >= t for every x in a set Z, then nu(Z) >= t H^n(Z). (Area) [Simon Ch. 2, Sect. 3; SimonGMT Chapter02.injective_area_formula_lipschitz_simon] for an injective Lipschitz map G : R^n -> R^(n+l) and Borel g >= 0, integral_{G(A)} g dH^n = integral_A g(G(x)) J_G(x) dx; for an injective linear map the same holds with constant Jacobian. (Rad) Rademacher's theorem (Mathlib LipschitzWith.ae_differentiableAt). (Leb) Lebesgue's differentiation theorem on R^n. (Cont) [sibling allard52_graph_plane_algebra, last conjunct] for each linear isometry q, the map B -> Pi_q(B) is continuous on the space of linear maps R^n -> R^l (directly: Pi_q(B) = q J_B (I + B^* B)^-1 J_B^* q^-1 with J_B v := graphPoint v (B v); each factor depends continuously on B and inversion is continuous on invertible operators).
Choice of constant; it depends only on n and p. Fix n >= 1 and p > n, and let delta_P, C_P be the constants of allard52_density_bounds for (n, p); they do not depend on l. Put delta_2 := delta_P, so 0 < delta_2 <= 1/8 and delta_2 depends only on n and p. Only now let l >= 0 be arbitrary. The steps below use delta only through delta <= delta_2 = delta_P (for (P.ii)) and delta <= 1/8; hence the same delta_2 works for every l, which is the statement with "there exists delta_2" placed before "for all l".

Let 0 < delta <= delta_2, 2.3 (AllardHypotheses H p delta rho), q, f, R with 0 < R <= delta rho, f(0) = 0, f 1-Lipschitz on B^n_R(0) and spt V cap B_R(0) = Gamma_R cap B_R(0).

1. Elementary facts. For x, x' in B^n_R(0): |F(x) - F(x')|^2 = |x - x'|^2 + |f(x) - f(x')|^2, so |x - x'| <= |F(x) - F(x')| <= sqrt 2 |x - x'|, and |F(x)| <= sqrt 2 |x| (f(0) = 0). F is injective on B^n_R(0), and its inverse on Gamma_R is the restriction of the 1-Lipschitz linear map a(w) := first n coordinates of q^-1 w; hence F maps L^n-null subsets of B^n_R(0) to H^n-null sets and a maps H^n-null subsets of Gamma_R to L^n-null sets. If x in B^o_{R/2}(0) then |F(x)| < R, so F(x) in Gamma_R cap B_R(0) = spt V cap B_R(0); thus F(B^o_{R/2}(0)) is contained in spt V cap B^o_R(0), and B_R(0) is contained in B_rho(0) (R <= delta rho <= rho/8), which is contained in U by 2.3.

2. Differentiability. Extend f restricted to B^n_R(0) to a Lipschitz map f~ : R^n -> R^l (componentwise McShane extension, Mathlib LipschitzOnWith.extend_pi; constant at most sqrt l); F~(x) := q(graphPoint x (f~ x)) is Lipschitz and injective on R^n. By (Rad), f is differentiable at L^n-a.e. x in B^o_R(0) (f = f~ near such x), and there DF(x)v = q(graphPoint v (Df(x)v)), DF(x)(R^n) = q(graph Df(x)) is n-dimensional, and J_F(x) = det(I + Df(x)^* Df(x))^(1/2) >= 1.

3. The carrier fills the graph. Let Z := (spt V cap B^o_R(0)) minus M. For y in Z we have |y| < R <= delta rho <= 3 delta rho, so by (P.ii) mu(B_s(y)) >= omega_n s^n/2 for all s in (0, rho/2]; for s < R - |y| the ball B_s(y) lies in B^o_R(0), so the finite Radon measure nu := mu restricted to B^o_R(0) satisfies Theta^{*n}(nu, y) >= 1/2 on Z. Since mu(R^(n+l) minus M) = 0, nu(Z) = 0, and (UD) gives H^n(Z) <= 2 nu(Z) = 0. Also H^n(M minus spt V) = 0 (mu(M minus spt V) = 0 because spt mu has full measure, and theta > 0 on M). Since spt V cap B^o_R(0) = Gamma_R cap B^o_R(0), the sets M cap B^o_R(0) and Gamma_R cap B^o_R(0) differ by an H^n-null set.

4. Multiplicity at least 1. N := {w in M : theta(w) < 1} satisfies mu(N) = integral_N theta dH^n = 0 by 2.3 (theta >= 1 mu-a.e.); as theta > 0 on N, H^n(N) = 0. Thus theta >= 1 H^n-a.e. on M.

5. Tangent planes along the graph. Claim: for L^n-a.e. x in B^o_{R/2}(0), if F(x) in M then f is differentiable at x and p_{F(x)} = Pi_q(Df(x)).
 Let theta~ := theta on M and theta~ := 1 off M, and g(x) := theta~(F(x)) J_F(x) on B^o_R(0). For compact K' contained in B^o_R(0), F(K') is compact and contained in B_{sqrt2 R}(0), which lies in B_rho(0) and hence in U (sqrt 2 R <= sqrt 2 delta rho < rho, as delta <= delta_2 <= 1/8), and by (Area) integral_{K'} g dx = integral_{F(K')} theta~ dH^n <= integral_{F(K') cap M} theta dH^n + H^n(F(K')) < infinity (theta is integrable on M cap F(K'); H^n(F(K')) < infinity since F is Lipschitz). Since theta is H^n-a.e.-measurable on M and a maps H^n-null sets to L^n-null sets, g is L^1_loc on B^o_R(0). Exclude the L^n-null set of x in B^o_{R/2}(0) at which f is not differentiable or x is not a Lebesgue point of g with value g(x) (Leb). Let x be any remaining point with y := F(x) in M, and let psi in C_c(R^(n+l)) with spt psi in B_rho'(0). For 0 < r < (R - |y|)/rho', the ball B_{r rho'}(y) lies in B^o_R(0), where M and Gamma_R agree up to H^n-null sets (step 3), so by the blow-up identity (H^n(y + r E) = r^n H^n(E)) and (Area) applied to F,
 integral_{eta_{y,r}(M)} psi(z) theta(y + r z) dH^n(z) = r^-n integral_M psi((w - y)/r) theta(w) dH^n(w) = r^-n integral_{Gamma_R} psi((w - y)/r) theta~(w) dH^n(w) = r^-n integral_{B^o_R(0)} psi((F(x') - F(x))/r) g(x') dx' = integral_{R^n} psi((F(x + r v) - F(x))/r) g(x + r v) dv,
 where the last integrand vanishes unless |v| <= rho' (because |F(x + r v) - F(x)| >= r|v|). As r -> 0, (F(x + r v) - F(x))/r -> DF(x)v uniformly for |v| <= rho' (differentiability), so psi((F(x + r v) - F(x))/r) -> psi(DF(x)v) uniformly there (psi is uniformly continuous and bounded), and integral_{B_rho'(0)} |g(x + r v) - g(x)| dv -> 0 (Lebesgue point). Hence the integral tends to g(x) integral psi(DF(x)v) dv = theta(y) J_F(x) integral psi(DF(x)v) dv = theta(y) integral_{q(graph Df(x))} psi dH^n by (Area) for the injective linear map DF(x). So the n-dimensional subspace q(graph Df(x)) is the approximate tangent space of M w.r.t. theta at y (Simon Ch. 3, Def. 1.7 = HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt). As theta(y) > 0 it is unique (SimonGMT HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique), so by the definition of V.tangentProj, p_y = Pi_q(Df(x)). This proves the claim.

6. Conclusion. Let Phi be jointly Borel, A a measurable subset of B^o_{R/2}(0). By step 1 F(A) is contained in spt V cap B^o_R(0). The set of x in A with F(x) not in M is mapped by F into Z, an H^n-null set (step 3), so it is L^n-null (a is Lipschitz). With steps 2 and 5, for L^n-a.e. x in A: F(x) in M, f is differentiable at x, J_F(x) >= 1 and p_{F(x)} = Pi_q(Df(x)). Therefore, using J_F >= 1, (Area) for the injective Lipschitz map F~ on A (F~ = F on A, with the same Jacobian at differentiability points of the open ball), step 3 (H^n(F(A) minus M) = 0), step 4 (theta >= 1 H^n-a.e. on M) and mu = theta H^n restricted to M:
 integral_A Phi(F(x), Pi_q(Df(x))) dx = integral_A Phi(F(x), p_{F(x)}) dx <= integral_A Phi(F(x), p_{F(x)}) J_F(x) dx = integral_{F(A)} Phi(w, p_w) dH^n(w) = integral_{F(A) cap M} Phi(w, p_w) dH^n(w) <= integral_{F(A) cap M} Phi(w, p_w) theta(w) dH^n(w) = integral_{F(A)} Phi(w, p_w) dmu(w).
 Measurability: (x, P) -> Phi(x, P) is Borel; x -> Pi_q(Df(x)) is Borel (fderiv is Borel measurable, Mathlib measurable_fderiv, and Pi_q is continuous by (Cont)); w -> p_w is mu-a.e. equal to a Borel map (T), and on F(A) cap M the null sets of mu and H^n coincide (theta > 0), so every integrand above is a.e.-measurable for the relevant measure, and the area formula applies to the composed Borel functions. The displayed chain is exactly the asserted inequality between lintegrals (the left side is the lintegral over A with respect to Lebesgue measure on R^n, the right side the lintegral over q '' graphOver f A with respect to mu). Since delta_2 was fixed from (n, p) before l, this proves the statement for every l.
key_steps: delta_2 := delta_P(n,p) from the uniform density bounds, fixed before the codimension l
The graph map F is bi-Lipschitz onto its image and F(B^o_{R/2}(0)) lies in spt V cap B^o_R(0)
Density lower bound (P.ii) and the density theorem give H^n((spt V cap B^o_R(0)) minus M) = 0
Blow-up through the area formula at differentiability and Lebesgue points identifies T_{F(x)}(M, theta) = q(graph Df(x))
Chain: J_F >= 1, area formula, H^n(F(A) minus M) = 0, theta >= 1
